newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Foreign investment in Bulgaria rises.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Bulgaria rises.

text.p: Direct foreign investment in Bulgaria for the first nine months of 1996 stood at $201 million, double the level for the same period last year, deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said on Friday.
"A total of 2,217 direct foreign investments worth $201.1 million were registered during the first nine months of this year," Gechev, who is also economy minister, told a news conference.
He said investment was twice what it had been in the same period last year but gave no figure.
Green field investment accounts for 40 percent. Foreign investment in government securities had also increased, he said, but he declined to elaborate.
The biggest two investments include a $22.3 million deal with South Korea's Daewoo Corp for 67 percent of Bulgaria's most luxurious hotel, the Sheraton Sofia.
The second is a 23.5 million mark deal under which German news organisation Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung bought 70 percent of Bulgaria's 168 Hours press group.
Germany is the biggest foreign investor in Bulgaria, holding 32 percent of all investments, said Gechev.
